Lesson preparation

Backwards planning / Begin with the end

Planning from the intended curriculum outcome or performance and working backwards to the prerequisite knowledge, intermediate steps, practice and assessment evidence.

Lesson preparation

Plan the explanation

Deliberately scripting the conceptual route, key language, examples, representations, misconceptions and stopping points before teaching new content.

Practical guidance↗
Lesson preparation

Plan the means of participation / Double plan

Planning both teacher actions and the cognitive actions students will take: thinking, retrieving, writing, discussing, explaining and revising.

Practical guidance↗
Lesson preparation

Plan the exemplar and plan the error

Preparing a high-quality model response and the misconceptions, weak examples or incorrect processes most likely to occur.

Practical guidance↗
Lesson preparation

Annotated seating plans and purposeful adult deployment

Using current knowledge of pupils to position students and adults deliberately, annotate practical supports, plan talk partners and define circulation or check routes.

Climate & Culture

Solid entry routines and threshold

A short, explicitly taught sequence for moving from corridor to classroom and beginning independent learning immediately.

Practical guidance↗
Climate & Culture

Signal for attention and habits of attention

A consistent cue followed by observable, inclusive attention behaviours that prepare students to listen, look or think about the intended content.

Practical guidance↗
Climate & Culture

Routines, transitions and precorrections

Teaching repeated classroom processes explicitly and priming students immediately before predictable difficulty points.

Practical guidance↗
Climate & Culture

Positive narration, precise praise and motivation

Reinforcing the actions, effort, quality and norms that support learning while building belonging, competence and value.

Practical guidance↗
Climate & Culture

Least-intrusive correction and behavioural leadership

A calm graduated response that starts with visibility, proximity or non-verbal cues and escalates only as needed while preserving dignity and learning time.

Practical guidance↗
Climate & Culture

Making participation safe

Designing predictable, high-success participation in which students can think, speak, practise and make mistakes without humiliation while expectations remain ambitious.

Practical guidance↗
Drive Thinking for All

Everyone, Together, Anyone (ETA) and active participation

A participation framework that moves between responses from everyone, structured thinking with a partner and individual accountability.

Practical guidance↗
Drive Thinking for All

Cold calling

Asking the question to the whole class, allowing thinking time and then warmly inviting a selected student to respond.

Practical guidance↗
Drive Thinking for All

Wait time

A deliberate pause after a question and a second pause after a student's response before the teacher evaluates or moves on.

Practical guidance↗
Drive Thinking for All

Call and response / Choral response

A clearly cued routine in which the whole class gives the same concise response in unison.

Practical guidance↗
Drive Thinking for All

Turn and Talk / Think-Pair-Share / Oracy

Structured talk that begins with individual thinking, uses a focused paired exchange and ends with accountable sharing, writing or rechecking.

Practical guidance↗
Drive Thinking for All

Second Chance / No Opt Out

Returning to a student who could not initially answer after giving them time and access to peer responses, so that they still complete an intellectually meaningful response.

Practical guidance↗
Drive Thinking for All

Process questions and equitable follow-up

Questions that probe how or why an answer was produced, ask for evidence, comparison or connection, and refine responses for precision.

Practical guidance↗
Drive Thinking for All

Mini-whiteboards for participation

A routine in which every student commits a short written, symbolic or multiple-choice response and reveals it on a common cue.

Practical guidance↗
Drive Thinking for All

Everybody Writes and accountable discussion

Using brief individual writing before or after talk so every student develops, records and revises an idea.

Practical guidance↗
Check & Adapt

Checking for understanding / TAPPLE

A continuous feedback loop in which teachers ask, pause, select a response method, listen or look, interpret the evidence and act.

Practical guidance↗
Check & Adapt

Hinge questions

A pre-planned diagnostic question at a critical point where the class response determines whether teaching moves on, consolidates or reteaches.

Practical guidance↗
Check & Adapt

Mini-whiteboards for diagnosis

Using standardised, simultaneous board responses to gather valid whole-class data quickly enough to adapt in the moment.

Practical guidance↗
Check & Adapt

Responsive thresholds and high success

Using approximate success bands to choose a proportionate response while keeping practice in a productive zone, commonly around 80% success.

Practical guidance↗
Check & Adapt

Responsive micro-decisions

A disciplined noticing-interpreting-responding cycle that asks whether understanding is secure, where the gap lies, whether to stay or pivot, whose thinking is missing and whether the response landed.

Practical guidance↗
Check & Adapt

Adaptive teaching: high challenge, responsive support

Maintaining a shared ambitious goal while adjusting explanation, representation, scaffolding, grouping, time or practice in response to barriers and live evidence.

Practical guidance↗
Check & Adapt

Checks for listening

Brief, planned prompts that require students to reproduce, reframe or act on what has just been said, showing whether attention became usable information.

Practical guidance↗
Do Now

Do Now: retrieval-rich lesson start

A short, immediately accessible and independently completed start-of-lesson routine, usually built around spaced retrieval rather than new content.

Practical guidance↗
Do Now

Retrieval practice: spacing, challenge and feedback

Effortfully recalling previously taught knowledge after some forgetting, with low stakes and feedback that makes the retrieval event itself part of learning.

Practical guidance↗
Explain

Activating prior knowledge

Bringing the specific existing knowledge needed for new learning into working memory and making the connection explicit.

Practical guidance↗
Explain

Small steps and precise explanation

Breaking complex content into coherent, cumulative units and explaining each with concise, accurate language before immediate guided practice.

Practical guidance↗
Explain

Cognitive simplicity in slides and resources

Designing explanations and materials so attention is directed to essential information: removing clutter, keeping related information together and retaining key transient information.

Practical guidance↗
Explain

Worked examples and providing models

Showing a complete or partially completed solution or product, with the structure, sequence and decisions made explicit before students perform independently.

Practical guidance↗
Explain

Thinking aloud

Verbalising the expert's internal decisions, monitoring and self-correction while completing a task.

Practical guidance↗
Explain

Examples, non-examples and variation

Choosing positive examples, near-miss non-examples and deliberately varied cases to reveal the defining features and boundaries of a concept.

Practical guidance↗
Explain

Visualiser, live drawing and dual coding

Constructing writing, annotation, diagrams or models live while directing attention and revealing the decisions behind the representation.

Practical guidance↗
Explain

Storytelling, analogies and memorable explanation

Using a concise narrative, analogy or metaphor to organise causal relationships and make an abstract idea easier to understand and remember.

Practical guidance↗
Explain

Explicit vocabulary instruction with active practice

Teaching a word's meaning, pronunciation, form, examples, non-examples and connections, followed by repeated retrieval and use in context.

Practical guidance↗
Secure learning through practice

Guided practice

Short supported rehearsal in which the teacher and students co-work examples, make responses visible and correct errors before independent release.

Practical guidance↗
Secure learning through practice

Purposeful independent practice

Independent rehearsal and application of explicitly taught knowledge or skills, designed for accuracy, fluency and increasing automaticity.

Practical guidance↗
Secure learning through practice

Scaffolding difficult tasks

Temporary support such as a model, worked example, prompt, sentence stem, vocabulary bank, partial task or visual cue that preserves the ambitious task.

Practical guidance↗
Secure learning through practice

Fading support and backward fading

Reducing a model or scaffold in small evidence-led steps, often removing the final step first while keeping the task and method stable.

Practical guidance↗
Secure learning through practice

Circulation and actionable live feedback

Purposeful movement through a planned route to scan, read, compare work with criteria and give brief feedback that prompts immediate improvement.

Practical guidance↗
Secure learning through practice

Practice for fluency, cumulative review and challenge

Sequencing repeated, varied and spaced opportunities so accurate knowledge or processes become increasingly fluent and can be applied in more complex contexts.

Practical guidance↗
Feedback to improve

Precise individual feedback

Brief information that identifies the exact gap and prompts the student to retrieve, correct, practise or improve while the work is still active.

Practical guidance↗
Feedback to improve

Whole-class feedback and Show Call

Reviewing a set of work to identify patterns, then teaching from common strengths, misconceptions and strategically selected examples rather than writing repeated individual comments.

Practical guidance↗
Feedback to improve

Structured peer feedback

Students use clear criteria and modelled language to identify a specific strength and an actionable improvement in a peer's work.

Practical guidance↗
Feedback to improve

Feedback as detective work

Diagnosing the underlying cause of a response before deciding what information, prompt, model or practice will move learning forward.

Practical guidance↗
Feedback to improve

Exit tickets and retrieval quizzes

Brief independent end-of-lesson or cumulative questions designed for rapid analysis and a clear instructional follow-up.

Practical guidance↗
Feedback to improve

Close the feedback loop: Own and Track

Ensuring students record the accurate answer, understand why it is accurate and visibly amend, annotate, redraft or re-practise their own work.

One-page strategy guide

LP01 · Planning backwards from what students need to learn

Use this when a lesson contains worthwhile activities but the knowledge students should leave with is unclear. Start with the intended learning, then select the explanation, practice and checks that will build it.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

LP02 · Prerequisite knowledge checks: identifying the foundations for new learning

Use this before new teaching when students need specific existing knowledge to access the explanation. Check the actual prerequisite rather than asking whether students remember last lesson.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

LP03 · Anticipating misconceptions and planning how to uncover them

Use this when students repeatedly make the same plausible error. Anticipate the reasoning behind that error so the lesson exposes and repairs it rather than merely announcing the correct answer.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

LP04 · Diagnostic questions: planning questions that reveal understanding

Use diagnostic questions when you need to see which misconception or decision is causing difficulty. A well-designed wrong option tells you something useful about students’ thinking.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

LP05 · Scaffolding: preparing support and deciding when to remove it

Use a scaffold when a specific barrier prevents students from attempting the intended learning successfully. Keep the goal clear and plan how students will work without the support.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CC01 · Entry routines: establishing a purposeful start

Use the agreed BSCS entry routine to make the move from corridor to independent learning warm, predictable and purposeful. Students should know where to go, what to prepare and how to begin.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CC02 · Teaching and rehearsing classroom routines

Use this when a repeated classroom process is unreliable. Routines become useful when students understand, practise and rehearse the exact actions, rather than hear a rule once.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CC03 · Signal for attention: securing readiness before teaching

Use the agreed BSCS signal before instructions, explanations and transitions. Secure readiness before speaking so the beginning of the message reaches the whole class.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CC04 · Checks for listening: instructions, explanations and classmates

Use brief checks to establish whether students heard the instruction, key explanation point or contribution from a classmate. This helps distinguish missed information from difficulty understanding it.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CC05 · Behaviour scripts: correcting calmly and precisely

Use calm, precise behaviour language to restore learning while preserving relationships. Apply the school behaviour system consistently and keep the response focused on the action that needs to change.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CC06 · Exit routines: ending lessons calmly and efficiently

Use the agreed BSCS exit sequence to finish learning, restore the room and move students calmly into the corridor. Plan sufficient time for practical equipment and resource return.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DN01 · Do Now: preparing students for learning

At BSCS, Do Now provides a short, independent start using spaced retrieval of previously taught, curriculum-critical knowledge. Keep the routine stable so thinking begins without a fresh explanation.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DN02 · Retrieval practice: strengthening recall

Use retrieval practice to strengthen access to previously taught knowledge. Students should attempt to generate the answer from memory before they see notes, prompts or the solution.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DN03 · Spaced retrieval: revisiting knowledge over time

Use spaced retrieval when students can answer soon after teaching but struggle weeks later. Plan repeated returns to important knowledge rather than treating a topic as finished.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DN04 · Low-stakes quizzes: making retrieval accessible and challenging

Use a recurring low-stakes quiz to revisit knowledge across topics and identify what each student needs to retrieve again. The review matters as much as the score.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DN05 · Do Now feedback: checking responses and addressing gaps

Use a proportionate review so Do Now both strengthens recall and informs teaching. Gather the answers first, then decide which items need confirmation, discussion or a brief repair.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

EX01 · Small steps: explaining new ideas in manageable chunks

Use small steps when several interacting decisions make new content hard to follow. Teach a coherent component, rehearse it and then connect it to the next part.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

EX02 · The visualiser: live modelling step by step

Use the visualiser to show how a response is constructed, including decisions, annotations and revisions. Students see the sequence that a finished example can hide.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

EX03 · Think aloud: making expert thinking visible

Use a think aloud when the important learning sits in the choices an expert makes. Show how you plan, monitor and evaluate, including why you reject an attractive alternative.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

EX04 · Examples and non-examples: clarifying what counts

Use examples and non-examples to make the defining feature of a concept clear. Carefully chosen near-misses help students stop relying on superficial appearance.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

EX05 · Dual coding: using diagrams and words together

Use words and visuals together when a diagram makes a relationship, sequence or structure easier to understand. Select the representation for its explanatory purpose.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

EX06 · Explicit vocabulary teaching: developing keystone vocabulary

Use explicit vocabulary teaching when disciplinary language is essential to understanding and expressing an idea. Students need to hear, say, use and revisit the word in context.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

EX07 · I Do We Do You Do: moving towards independence

Use I Do, We Do, You Do to move students from observing a clear model to accurate independence. The phases may repeat; readiness determines the handover.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

PR01 · Guided practice: checking readiness for independent work

Use guided practice when students have seen an explanation but are not yet ready to perform independently. Keep the demand closely aligned with the model and inspect each important decision.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

PR02 · Completion problems: bridging modelling and independence

Use completion problems to bridge a full worked example and an independent solution. Keep part of the successful structure visible while students supply the missing decisions.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

PR03 · Fading scaffolds: removing support as students become secure

Use fading to move students beyond dependence on prompts, models or frames. Decide which support to remove from evidence of what students can now do.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

PR04 · Fluency practice: securing the essential steps

Use fluency practice when students understand a process but perform it slowly or inconsistently. Secure accuracy before increasing pace, volume or complexity.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

PR05 · Variation: changing examples to deepen understanding

Use variation to help students notice the structure of an idea rather than copy surface features. Decide what changes, what stays the same and why that comparison matters.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

PR06 · Interleaving: practising how to choose an approach

Use interleaving when students can perform several approaches separately but need practice deciding which one fits. Mix types that require a meaningful choice after initial teaching.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

PR07 · Independent practice: helping students begin and sustain effort

Use independent practice to build accurate, sustained performance after explanation and guided rehearsal. Plan the launch, first items and monitoring so students remain thinking throughout.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DT01 · Wait time: giving everyone time to think

Use wait time to give everyone a chance to retrieve, reason and prepare an answer. Include a pause after a student response before immediately evaluating or asking someone else.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DT02 · Cold calling: involving everyone in questioning

Use cold calling to make classroom questions an invitation for everyone to think. Build a warm, predictable question–pause–name routine and use answers to guide teaching.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DT03 · Think Pair Share: preparing everyone to answer

Use Think–Pair–Share when students need independent thinking and private rehearsal before a public response. Protect the Think stage so the quickest speaker does not supply everyone’s first idea.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DT04 · Turn and Talk: structuring purposeful partner discussion

Use Turn and Talk for a short, purposeful exchange that helps students clarify or rehearse an idea. Specify the question, partner roles, time and response you will collect afterwards.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DT05 · Choral response: rehearsing brief answers together

Use choral response for brief, unambiguous answers that benefit from shared rehearsal. Teach a precise cue so students begin together rather than copying the earliest voice.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DT06 · Probing questions: moving beyond the first answer

Use probing questions after students have relevant knowledge to deepen or clarify the reasoning behind an answer. Plan a focused follow-up rather than asking a vague “Why?” every time.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

DT07 · Compare justify evaluate: questions that deepen reasoning

Use comparison, justification and evaluation prompts when students need to explain a relationship or make a judgement. Ensure they have the knowledge and criteria required to reason well.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CA01 · Mini-whiteboards: checking everyone's understanding

Make every student’s answer visible, identify gaps and decide what to teach next. Useful before independent practice or whenever answers from a few students leave you unsure about everyone else.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CA02 · Hinge questions: deciding whether to move on

Use a hinge question at a decision point where students’ answers should change what happens next. Plan the question and the teaching response together.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CA03 · Checking for understanding during explanations

Use checks during and between explanation chunks to find out what students can recall, distinguish or apply. Gather evidence that informs a specific teaching decision.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CA04 · Circulation: sampling independent work and responding

Use circulation to read learning across the room, identify the exact error and choose a response. Move with a route and a diagnostic focus rather than following raised hands alone.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CA05 · Exit tickets: identifying what needs revisiting

Use an exit ticket when a brief independent response can inform the next lesson. Choose essential knowledge and a format that can be reviewed quickly.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CA06 · Pause and Fix: responding to a common misconception

Use Pause & Fix when a common gap means continuing would reinforce an error or make the next step inaccessible. Stop briefly, repair the precise issue and return to a fresh attempt.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

CA07 · Adapt and Support Extend and Challenge: responding to different needs

Use Adapt & Support and Extend & Challenge when responses show different needs. Keep the learning goal ambitious while adjusting the support or depth of the next task.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

FI01 · Actionable feedback: giving students a useful next step

Use individual feedback when a precise next action can improve work while the thinking is still live. Make the location, learning issue and required change clear.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

FI02 · Whole-class feedback: responding to patterns in work

Use whole-class feedback when students’ work reveals shared strengths and recurring difficulties. Review the pattern once, then give everyone a useful improvement task.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

FI03 · Self-checking: teaching students to improve their own work

Use self-checking when students know what quality looks like but do not yet inspect their own work reliably. Teach a specific checking action rather than telling them to “check it”.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

FI04 · Peer critique: using criteria to improve work

Use peer critique when students understand the content and criteria well enough to offer accurate, useful feedback. Teach the feedback routine before exchanging work.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

FI05 · Feedback tasks: planning time to act on feedback

Use feedback tasks to make improvement an act of thinking. Select a solvable challenge that helps students locate, explain and repair an issue rather than simply copy a correction.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

FI06 · Feedback follow-up: checking improvement on a new task

Use feedback follow-up to find out whether the learning improved beyond the original correction. A new attempt gives more useful evidence than a rewritten answer alone.

PDF and Word available↗
One-page strategy guide

EX08 · Worked examples: showing a complete solution

Use a worked example when students need to see the full structure of a successful response before attempting a complex task. Make the important decisions and criteria visible.

PDF and Word available↗

FI07 · The visualiser: discussing and improving student work
